Walking Intervention — Pre/Post

Walking Intervention vs Control — Multimodal Results

Preliminary · cohort 107 structural / ~46 FC-EC / ~39 voxelwise subjects · all group×time interactions · FDR or cluster-corrected · effective connectivity via rDCM/VAR/Granger/K-SG TE

Headline: the walking intervention preserves subcortical volume (amygdala, thalamus, putamen, hippocampus) and increases cerebellar directed/functional connectivity, while cortical thickness is unchanged.

Cohort & coverage

Two-timepoint subjects (Control vs Walking), mean-FD>0.3mm excluded. Structural analyses use the full cohort; FC/EC use the subset with complete XCP-D data; voxelwise (ALFF/ReHo/seed-to-voxel) are old-cohort pending rerun.

Full ROI-to-ROI (442×442) + NBS

No significant connected subnetworks (NBS cluster p > 0.89 at t=3.0 and t=2.5). The intervention's FC changes are diffuse — summary-level effects survive, coherent edge-clusters do not.

97,461 edges, delta (post−pre), two-sample t-test, Network-Based Statistic cluster correction (5,000 permutations).

Effective connectivity

Directed connectivity on the 9 network blocks (Yeo 7 + subcortex + cerebellum), ec-variant denoised BOLD (0.01–0.1 Hz, 0 mm smoothing). LMM per edge ~ group×time + Age + Gender + (1|subject), BH-FDR. Four methods compared. TR=0.8 s → HRF-latency confounded; hypothesis-generating, non-causal.

Structural connectivity (dMRI)

Pending. QSIPrep preprocessing was ~98/108 complete at report time; QSIRecon (SS3T + ACT-hsvs) and the connectome matrices have not yet been generated. This tab will be populated when the dMRI pipeline completes.

Methods

Cohort & design

Longitudinal walking intervention, 2 groups (Walking vs Control) × 2 timepoints (pre = ses-01, post = ses-02). All models estimate the group×time interaction (differential change between groups). Mean-FD > 0.3 mm excluded.

Preprocessing

  • fMRIPrep 25.2.5 (MNI152NLin6Asym res-2; no recon-all)
  • XCP-D 26.0.2 — fc variant: aCompCor, FD scrubbing (>0.3mm), bandpass 0.01–0.08 Hz, 6 mm smoothing; ec variant: aCompCor, bandpass 0.01–0.1 Hz, 0 mm smoothing. Confounds regressed at this stage; no re-regression downstream.
  • FastSurfer 2.5.4 for subcortical volumes / cortical thickness

Functional connectivity

442-parcel atlas (Schaefer400 + Tian subcortex + 10 cerebellar). Fisher-z matrices. Summary metrics: within/between-network z, ROI-to-network z, ROI-to-whole-brain z, graph metrics, 9-block partial correlation. LMM per metric ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject).

Effective connectivity

Four methods on the 9 network blocks (Yeo 7 + subcortex + cerebellum) and on the 15-block cerebellum-Yeo split: VAR(1) A-matrix (multivariate linear directed connectivity), rDCM (regression dynamic causal modelling, TAPAS/Julia, Wiener stochastic input, 16 samples/TR), pairwise Granger (bivariate F-statistic), KSG transfer entropy (kNN, k=4). All are HRF-latency confounded at TR=0.8 s → hypothesis-generating.

Voxelwise / seed-to-voxel

ALFF/ReHo (voxelwise), seed-to-voxel Pearson→Fisher-z. Per-subject delta (post−pre) maps; two-sample t-test via FSL randomise, TFCE, 5000 permutations. Cluster composition via FSL atlasq + AAL3v1 (covers cortex, subcortex and cerebellum).

Corrections & caveats

  • BH-FDR within families; NBS cluster-level FWER (5,000 perms) for full ROI-to-ROI; TFCE for voxelwise.
  • LMM fitted with BFGS (L-BFGS produced singular-Hessian failures on a subset of edges, silently dropping tests).
  • Preliminary — no permutation max-T at the summary level, no split-half replication.
  • EC results non-causal; spectral DCM (SPM) would be the confirmatory step.
